title: From Bathtub to World Cup Final: The Photographer Behind Messi and Yamal's Iconic 2007 Photo
excerpt: Photographer Joan Monfort captured the iconic Messi-Yamal photo in 2007 for a UNICEF charity calendar.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Photographer Joan Monfort captured the iconic Messi-Yamal photo in 2007 for a UNICEF charity calendar.
  • The photo gained viral attention during Euro 2024, shared by Yamal's father on Instagram.
  • Monfort expresses frustration over the widespread sharing of the photo without credit.
  • The upcoming World Cup final features Messi and Yamal, highlighting their generational connection.
The Iconic Charity Photo
›Captured in December 2007 by Joan Monfort.
›Part of a UNICEF charity calendar organized by Sport.
›Yamal's mother won a raffle to meet Messi.
›Yamal was just a few months old during the shoot.
Source: Associated Press

  • Photographer Joan Monfort, who captured the 2007 charity photo of Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal, says his "heart is breaking in two pieces" ahead of Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain.
  • The photos were taken for a UNICEF charity calendar organized by Barcelona newspaper Sport, after Yamal's mother won a raffle in Mataro pairing her baby son with the then-rising Barcelona star.
  • The images went viral during Euro 2024 when Yamal's father shared them on Instagram, and have attracted even greater global attention ahead of the 2026 World Cup final.
  • Monfort has expressed frustration that the photos are widely shared online without proper credit or permission.

A photograph taken nearly two decades ago showing a young Lionel Messi bathing an infant Lamine Yamal has taken on extraordinary significance ahead of Sunday's FIFA World Cup final, where the Argentine legend and the Spanish prodigy will face each other for football's biggest prize.

The image has become one of football's most extraordinary visual artefacts — proof, if anyone needed it, that the sport writes scripts no screenwriter would dare attempt.

The Charity Photo Shoot That Started It All

The now-iconic images were captured in December 2007 by Barcelona-based freelance photographer Joan Monfort. The occasion was a charity calendar organized by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF, in which Barcelona players posed with young children and their families at Camp Nou's visitors' locker room.

Yamal's mother, Sheila, had won a raffle in their hometown of Mataro, near Barcelona, that allowed families to take part in the project. By pure chance, her infant son — just a few months old at the time — was paired with Messi, then a 20-year-old rising star at the club.

"I never believed in destiny, but this is beyond explanation," Monfort told the Associated Press from Barcelona this week.

From Forgotten Photo to Global Phenomenon

The images remained largely forgotten for more than 15 years. They resurfaced during the UEFA Euro 2024 tournament, when Yamal's father Mounir Nasraoui shared one of them on Instagram with the caption: "The beginning of two legends." Yamal, then 16, was playing a key role in Spain's title-winning campaign, having scored a world-class goal against France in the semifinals.

UNICEF confirmed the photos' authenticity, with UNICEF Catalonia's Laia Ruich noting that "the photographer has said that Lamine Yamal stole Messi's heart because he was always smiling."

The photo quickly went viral and has attracted even greater global attention ahead of the World Cup final. Monfort said media requests for the photographs have surged in recent days.

"It feels better than any movie script."

— Joan Monfort, photographer

A Photographer's Impossible Choice

As a lifelong Barcelona supporter, Monfort admitted he faces an impossible choice on Sunday. Like many Barcelona fans, he remains deeply attached to Messi — who left the club in 2021 amid financial difficulties — while also embracing Yamal as the club's next generation of talent.

"I have everlasting admiration for Messi, the greatest player of all time," Monfort said. "But Yamal has broken the mould and represents a new generation."

Yamal himself has spoken about the photo in interviews, revealing he had no idea about it until his father showed it to him. "I never have been able to speak with him about it. I wish I could have spoken with him, but I never have," Yamal said in an interview. "The first person to show me the photo was my father, and we never made it public because, in the end, we didn't want comparisons between Leo and me."

Diaspora Angle

For Indian football fans — a growing community with deep connections to both La Liga and the World Cup — the Messi-Yamal story resonates as a narrative of mentorship, legacy, and the unpredictable arc of sporting greatness. Indian viewership of the 2026 World Cup has shattered records, and the final between Argentina and Spain promises to be one of the most-watched events in the country's history.

What's Next

The World Awaits
›Argentina vs. Spain in World Cup final on Sunday.
›Messi seeks record third World Cup title at age 39.
›Yamal, at 19, aims to be one of the youngest winners.
›Indian viewership for the World Cup has shattered records.

Argentina face Spain in the World Cup final on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Messi, at 39, is seeking a record third World Cup title. Yamal, at 19, would become one of the youngest players ever to win the tournament. Whether watching from New Jersey or Barcelona, Monfort said choosing between the two won't be easy.

"My heart is divided," he said. "Maybe they can both win. After everything that has happened, I wouldn't rule anything out."
